title: Finite-presentation tensor models for an invertible module and its dual
statement: Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(Z_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact schemes [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] that are quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], with affine transition morphisms $q_{ji}:Z_j\to Z_i$ for $j\geq i$ [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $Z=\varprojlim_i Z_i$ with projections $q_i:Z\to Z_i$ be its limit in the category of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Here being a limit means $q_{ji}\circ q_j=q_i$ for $j\geq i$, and for every scheme $T$ and family $t_i:T\to Z_i$ satisfying $q_{ji}\circ t_j=t_i$ there is a unique morphism $t:T\to Z$ with $q_i\circ t=t_i$ for every $i$. For a sheaf of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], finite presentation means that every point has an open neighbourhood $U$ on which there is an exact sequence $\mathcal O_U^m\to\mathcal O_U^n\to F|_U\to0$ for finite $m,n$. All pullbacks are tensor pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback], with iterated pullbacks identified by their canonical composition isomorphisms. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] and put $N=L^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Z}(L,\mathcal O_Z)$. Then $N$ is invertible, $L$ and $N$ are finitely presented, and evaluation $e:L\otimes N\to\mathcal O_Z$ is an isomorphism. There exist $i\in I$, finitely presented $\mathcal O_{Z_i}$-modules $A_i,B_i$, and isomorphisms $a:q_i^*A_i\xrightarrow{\sim}L$, $b:q_i^*B_i\xrightarrow{\sim}N$. The sheaves $P_i=A_i\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Z_i}}B_i$ and $\mathcal O_{Z_i}$ are finitely presented. Here $\otimes$ is the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The composite $$\epsilon:q_i^*P_i\xrightarrow{\sim}q_i^*A_i\otimes q_i^*B_i\xrightarrow{a\otimes b}L\otimes N\xrightarrow{e}\mathcal O_Z$$ is an isomorphism, where the first arrow is the canonical pullback-tensor comparison. Neither invertibility nor local freeness of $A_i$ or $B_i$ is asserted.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible] with $\mathcal M=\mathcal N=L$: its dual clause makes $N=L^\vee$ invertible and its evaluation clause gives the specified isomorphism $e:L\otimes N\to\mathcal O_Z$. By [def-sc-invertible-module], each of $L,N$ is locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_Z$. On a trivializing open, the sequence $\mathcal O^0\to\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\sim}L\to0$ (and likewise for $N$) is a finite presentation. This proves all the assertions about $L,N,e$ before descent.

Apply clause (1) of [lem-trf-fp-modules-affine-limit-descent] separately to $L$ and $N$. It gives indices $r,s$, finitely presented models $A_r,B_s$, and pullback isomorphisms to $L,N$. Choose a common upper bound $i\geq r,s$ by directedness, and put $A_i=q_{ir}^*A_r$, $B_i=q_{is}^*B_s$. Both are finitely presented by [lem-pc-tensor-pullback-finite-presentation], which requires no flatness. The composition isomorphisms of [def-pc-module-pullback] identify $q_i^*A_i$ with $q_r^*A_r$, and $q_i^*B_i$ with $q_s^*B_s$, since $q_{ir}\circ q_i=q_r$ and $q_{is}\circ q_i=q_s$. Compose with the chosen isomorphisms to obtain $a,b$. All qcqs and affine-transition hypotheses of the descent lemma are precisely the hypotheses of this item.

Apply [lem-trf-fp-sheaf-tensor-product] on $Z_i$ to the finitely presented $A_i,B_i$. It gives finite presentation of $P_i=A_i\otimes B_i$, without an invertibility or flatness hypothesis on either factor. The structure module has the global finite presentation $\mathcal O_{Z_i}^0\to\mathcal O_{Z_i}\xrightarrow{1}\mathcal O_{Z_i}\to0$.

The canonical isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor], applied to $q_i,A_i,B_i$, gives $q_i^*P_i\cong q_i^*A_i\otimes q_i^*B_i$. Tensoring the isomorphisms $a,b$ gives an isomorphism: the tensor of their inverses is its inverse by functoriality of tensor. Composing with $e$ gives exactly the displayed $\epsilon$, so $\epsilon$ is an isomorphism. This only uses the evaluation isomorphism on the limit and makes no assertion that either finite-stage model is locally free.

lean.statement: theorem invertible_fp_tensor_models {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}) [∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, CompactSpace (D.obj i)] [∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)] [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map f)] (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (L : c.pt.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] : (dual L).IsInvertible ∧ L.IsFinitePresentation ∧ (dual L).IsFinitePresentation ∧ IsIso (dualEvaluation L) ∧ ∃ (i : I) (A B : (D.obj (op i)).Modules), A.IsFinitePresentation ∧ B.IsFinitePresentation ∧ ∃ (a : (tensorPullback (c.π.app (op i))).obj A ≅ L) (b : (tensorPullback (c.π.app (op i))).obj B ≅ dual L), (A ⊗ B).IsFinitePresentation ∧ (𝟙_ (D.obj (op i)).Modules).IsFinitePresentation ∧ IsIso ((Classical.choose (module_pullback_tensor (c.π.app (op i))) A B).hom ≫ (a.hom ⊗ₘ b.hom) ≫ dualEvaluation L)
